arguments.conclusion: The US government's current debt-to-GDP ratio is unsustainable due to insufficient tax revenue, large deficits, and the inability to lower interest rates without inflation.
source_speech_filenames: 20260216_The New Fed Chair’s Plan to Reduce the National Debt.txt
arguments.premise_synthesis: The debt-to-GDP ratio after WWII was 121% and after falling to about 30% by the early 1980s has returned to similar high levels over the last 40 years. There is not enough money in the economy to tax sufficiently to pay for government bills. The US government runs very large deficits every year, resulting in high interest rate costs. The Fed cannot lower interest rates without risking hyperinflation, which constrains monetary policy options.
arguments.conclusion_supported: This argument establishes that the current debt-to-GDP ratio is at historically high and unsustainable levels given insufficient tax revenue and persistent deficits, and that the Fed is constrained from lowering interest rates, which would otherwise risk inflation—a specific instance of the central claim that deficit spending forces the Fed to adopt unconventional policies.
